issues.problem: ctx1 and ctx2 (broke a cup and kept watching TV; went back to work after criticism) could take 满不在乎 just as well.
issues.action: Rewrote both to show outward calm hiding something (afraid Mum finds out; eyes red but acting normal).

issues.problem: bad2 (他对这件事若无其事) is only awkward, not clearly wrong, and the reason given was weak.
issues.action: Replaced with 激动得若无其事, which contradicts the idiom's meaning of looking calm and unaffected.

issues.problem: ctx6 (两个队的水平…) could take 不相上下 equally well.
issues.action: Rewrote with the mocking frame 谁也别笑谁 so only the 'both equally bad' idiom fits.

issues.problem: ctx5 (worries vanished at once) is the typical slot for 烟消云散, which is in the set.
issues.action: Replaced with a boat vanishing from sight on the sea; added 烟消云散 to near with the difference.

issues.problem: ctx6 (throwing a loyal servant out) describes actively harming a benefactor, which is 恩将仇报 or 忘恩负义, not 不知好歹.
issues.action: Rewrote: the young master scolds the servant who gave him well-meant advice.

issues.problem: ctx5 (drawn into a shop by the smell of bread) could take 情不自禁 just as well.
issues.action: Replaced with turning one's head on hearing one's name, a reflex.

issues.problem: ctx4 (nobody could get a word in) has a critical tone that fits 喋喋不休 just as well.
issues.action: Rewrote to show fluent talk: speaking for an hour and reeling off figures.

issues.problem: Story check: all ten stories are null. None of these idioms has a well-known origin tale.
issues.action: Left all stories as null. Meanings, registers, cues, parts and the other misuses were checked and kept.
